title: WAL commit-path bundle: buffer capacity, writer cadence, flush batching, group commit, compression
configuration_cause: wal_buffers=512 (4MB) with wal_writer_delay=200ms and commit_delay=0 forces each committing backend to self-flush; wal_waiting_backends spikes to 2 and wal_sync_time_per_txn=1.16ms dominates the 0.14ms sync average, while wal_compression=off leaves FPI volume (0.000143 FPI/txn) uncompressed.
mechanism: The WAL commit path is under-provisioned: small wal_buffers plus a 200ms writer cadence means backends frequently find no pre-flushed WAL and must issue their own fsync, producing wal_wait queueing. Enlarging wal_buffers to 2048 (16MB) absorbs bursts; shortening wal_writer_delay to 20ms and lowering wal_writer_flush_after to 0 lets the writer flush promptly so commits find WAL already durable; a small commit_delay=100us with commit_siblings=2 collects concurrent committers into one fsync; wal_compression=on shrinks FPI WAL bytes, reducing write/sync volume. Together these cut per-commit sync frequency and queueing, freeing terminal capacity for GetUserTweets.
query_effect: InsertTweet commits (the only WAL-generating path) should complete with fewer self-issued fsyncs; GetUserTweets read latency is unaffected directly but benefits from reduced backend contention on the WAL writer lock.
expected_tps_effect: Modest increase (0.5-2%) via reduced commit-path queueing and lower WAL volume; primary gain is lower InsertTweet tail latency.
expected_latency_effect: InsertTweet p95/p99 decrease; overall p95 roughly unchanged since GetUserTweets dominates terminal capacity.

knob_changes.numerical_basis: 4x current 4MB to 16MB, at safe high bound 2048 (8kB units); absorbs commit bursts without exceeding shared_buffers headroom.
Lower to safe low bound 20ms so the writer flushes WAL before backends arrive; 10x faster cadence.
0 disables forced flush-after, letting the writer flush on its own cadence rather than at 1MB boundaries; safe low bound.
100us collection window is well under the 0.14ms sync average, so it can batch concurrent committers into one fsync without adding net latency; safe range [0,1000].
Lower activation threshold to 2 so group commit engages with the observed 4-6 active backends; safe range [0,20].
Enable to compress full-page images; observed 0.000143 FPI/txn and 4.8 WAL bytes/txn mean FPI dominates WAL volume, so compression reduces write/sync bytes.

predictions.rationale: Larger wal_buffers + faster writer cadence + group commit reduce backends waiting on WAL flush.
Group commit batches multiple committers per fsync, lowering average sync time per commit.
wal_compression=on compresses FPI, reducing WAL bytes per transaction.
Reduced commit-path queueing frees terminal capacity, raising completed transaction throughput.

alternatives.statement: If the bottleneck is purely WAL buffer capacity, raising wal_buffers alone (without writer cadence/group commit changes) would reduce wal_waiting_backends but leave sync_average_ms unchanged.
If FPI volume dominates, wal_compression=on alone would cut wal_bytes_per_txn by >20% while sync_average_ms stays flat.

why_exceeds_incumbent: Incumbent leaves the WAL commit path at defaults (small buffers, 200ms writer cadence, no group commit, no compression) despite a high-severity wal_wait alert and 1.16ms sync_time_per_txn. This coherent bundle addresses the diagnosed mechanism directly, targeting the only WAL-generating transaction (InsertTweet) without disturbing the read-dominated GetUserTweets path that drives terminal capacity.

nodes.label: WAL commit-path bundle: wal_buffers 2048, wal_writer_delay 20, wal_writer_flush_after 0, commit_delay 100, commit_siblings 2, wal_compression on
Pre-flushed WAL + group commit + compressed FPI reduce per-commit fsync frequency and queueing

cross_domain_requirements: concurrency_maintenance: confirm max_pred_locks_* remain non-binding under SERIALIZABLE before attributing retries to WAL
